concepts.def: Form 1 mol from elements at std state.
Complete combustion of 1 mol in O2.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Energy change when 1 mol of a compound forms from its elements in standard states at 298 K and 100 kPa.

Example: C(s) + O2(g) -> CO2(g), ΔHf = -394 kJ/mol. Note: oxygen written as O2(g) (its standard state).

1 mol substance reacted completely with oxygen. Products: CO2(g), H2O(l) (when applicable).

CH4(g) + 2O2(g) -> CO2(g) + 2H2O(l), ΔHc = -890 kJ/mol.

Energy when acid and base react to form 1 mol of water under standard conditions.

HCl(aq) + NaOH(aq) -> NaCl(aq) + H2O(l), ΔH_neut ~ -57 kJ/mol. Always exothermic. Strong acid/strong base values consistent.
